visual_goal: Show the finance core at the centre with specialist satellites around it, each attached by one owned interface arrow, and the e-invoicing gateway as a single box.
prompt: A hub-and-spoke illustration on a wide canvas. In the centre, a large solid open-book ledger on a platform labeled 'Finance core'. Arranged in a ring around it, eight smaller rounded boxes, each joined to the centre by exactly one arrow with a small padlock-shaped connector on it, showing a contracted interface: at the top left 'Tax engine', at the top 'E-invoicing gateway', at the top right 'Treasury', at the right 'Data platform', at the bottom right 'Consolidation', at the bottom 'Disclosure', at the bottom left 'Expenses', at the left 'Source-to-pay'. Arrows from 'Source-to-pay' and 'Expenses' point into the centre; arrows from the centre point out to 'Tax engine', 'E-invoicing gateway', 'Treasury', 'Data platform' and 'Consolidation'; one arrow goes from 'Consolidation' to 'Disclosure'. Two outer elements at the edge of the canvas: above 'E-invoicing gateway' a government building labeled 'Tax authorities' with one arrow from the gateway into it; to the right of 'Treasury' a group of three plain bank buildings labeled once 'Banks' with a two-way arrow between 'Treasury' and the banks. A double-headed arrow between 'Treasury' and the centre.
alt: The finance core ledger at the centre, ringed by satellites for tax, e-invoicing, treasury, data, consolidation, disclosure, expenses and source-to-pay, each attached by one interface arrow, with tax authorities and banks at the edge.

visual_goal: Show two tax call paths through one adapter: estimates at checkout that may fall back to a flagged cached rate, commits that wait and retry, and the engine's journal reconciled to the ledger.
prompt: A left-to-right illustration with three vertical zones. At the far left, two stacked callers: on top a shopping cart screen labeled 'Checkout', below it a document tray labeled 'Invoicing'. In the centre, one single tall gatehouse spanning the full height of the canvas, labeled once 'Tax adapter'; it is the only gatehouse in the picture. At the right, one calculator machine labeled 'Tax engine', level with the middle of the gatehouse. Upper lane: a pair of arrows between 'Checkout' and the gatehouse, one going in and one coming back; a pair of arrows between the gatehouse and 'Tax engine', one going in and one coming back. A small yellow sticky note with a red flag labeled 'provisional rate' rides on the arrow coming back to 'Checkout'. Lower lane: a pair of arrows between 'Invoicing' and the gatehouse, one going in and one coming back; beside the gatehouse in this lane a small circular retry arrow icon labeled 'hold and retry'. Bottom row, running along the full width under everything: at the bottom left an open book labeled 'Ledger', with one arrow down from 'Invoicing' into it; at the bottom right a document stack labeled 'tax journal', with one arrow down from 'Tax engine' into it; and in the bottom centre, directly under the gatehouse, a balance-scale icon labeled 'reconcile', with one horizontal line from 'Ledger' to the left pan of the scale and one horizontal line from 'tax journal' to the right pan, so the scale weighs the two against each other.
alt: Checkout and invoicing both call the tax engine through one tax adapter; estimates can fall back to a flagged provisional rate, commits hold and retry, and the engine's tax journal is reconciled against the ledger.

visual_goal: Show that an invoice exists only once the tax authority accepts it: accepted invoices are posted and delivered, rejected ones go back for correction, and the gateway archives the cleared legal original.
prompt: A left-to-right flow illustration. At the far left a document box labeled 'Invoicing'. Next, a gateway arch labeled 'E-invoicing gateway', with an arrow from 'Invoicing' into it. Next, a plain generic office building labeled 'Provider', with an arrow from the gateway into it. At the right, a government building with columns labeled 'Tax authority', with an arrow from 'Provider' into it. From 'Tax authority' a road forks into two: an upper green path marked with a large green tick labeled 'accepted', and a lower red path marked with a red cross labeled 'rejected'. The green path leads to two destinations at the top right: an open book labeled 'Ledger' with a small stamp reading 'issued', and an unlabeled person at a desk receiving an envelope labeled 'Customer'. The red path curves all the way back along the bottom of the canvas into 'Invoicing', labeled 'correct and resubmit'. Under the gateway a small archive box with a sealed document labeled 'legal original'.
alt: An invoice passes from invoicing through the e-invoicing gateway and provider to the tax authority; accepted invoices are posted as issued and delivered to the customer, rejected ones return for correction, and the gateway archives the legal original.

visual_goal: Show the payment factory: the ledger decides what to pay, the factory screens, approves and routes to banks, and status and statements flow back so ledger, bank and cash position agree, proven by reconciliation.
prompt: A left-to-right flow illustration with a return loop. At the far left, two small boxes stacked: 'Source-to-pay' on top and 'Expenses' below, each with one arrow into a box next to them labeled 'Accounts payable'. Next, a large factory building labeled 'Payment factory', with an arrow from 'Accounts payable' into it labeled 'payment run'. Inside or directly in front of the factory a checkpoint with a shield and two approval ticks labeled 'screening and approval'. At the far right, a group of three plain bank buildings labeled once 'Banks', with a thick arrow from the factory into the banks carrying coins. Return loop along the bottom: two arrows from 'Banks' back into the factory, one labeled 'status' and one labeled 'statements'. From the factory: one arrow back left into 'Accounts payable' labeled 'status'; one arrow down to a box labeled 'Statement posting', which has one arrow on to a balance-scale icon labeled 'Bank reconciliation'; and one arrow up to an unlabeled small group of people beside a gauge labeled 'cash position'.
alt: Accounts payable sends payment runs into a payment factory that screens, approves and pays the banks; status and statements return to the factory, which updates payables, posts statements for bank reconciliation and reports the cash position to treasury.
